g_roast: Eighteen years in the grid, crew, and I never saw a load-in this badly organised. Even the opera tenors were tidier.
If this party were a truss, I'd refuse to stand under it. Nobody would get the insurance.
g_fire_back: Big words from somebody who tied that rope off with a bow, like a birthday present.
Careful, crew, I've fallen forty feet and landed in a tree. You don't scare me.
g_pile_on: And then they stood right under the falling rock and only looked up after it landed. A classic, that.
Worse than that, I watched it. They checked the knot, nodded, and it was still a bad knot.
lines.g_peacemake: Right, both of you, down tools for a minute. Sit, have a drink, and we sort it before the next lift, not during.
lines.g_take_side: Sorry, but this one's right. I looked at the whole rig, and their load path is the safe one.
lines.g_left_out: You two are on your own channel, that's fine. I'll go check some knots, there are always knots.
lines.g_include: Come here, grab a seat, there's room. Nobody stands around on my crew.
lines.g_bad_plan: Here's my plan, crew. Everyone climbs at once, nobody ties off, and we hope gravity's having a day off.
lines.g_plan_yes: Good plan, clean load path, I like it. Places, then, and we go when I say go.
lines.g_plan_no: No, that rig doesn't hold, I can see it from here. Somebody ends up under it, and it won't be pretty.
lines.g_hype: Right, crew, places, heads up, and nobody walks under anything. Going up on three.
lines.g_toast: Short one, I promise, the beer's getting warm. To my crew, the best I've had since the arena tours.
lines.g_cheers: Na zdravi, everyone, to your health. First round's on the guy who fell out of the sky.
g_quiet_line: My shoulder says rain tomorrow, by the way. It's never been wrong yet.
Somebody's tent is tied off with a granny knot. Not naming names, but it's going to fly away tonight.
lines.g_after_wipe: Okay, everyone up, slowly, check your gear. We dropped the load, it happens, and now we work out which knot slipped.
lines.g_crew: Eighteen years I always wanted the next tour, the next city. Lately I just want the next job with this crew.
lines.g_exasperated: I explained the whole plan before the fight, slowly, with drawings. And every one of you did it backwards, sakra.
lines.g_love_sharp: You spot the weak point in the rig before anybody else. That's the most useful eye on any crew.
lines.g_love_kind: You look up for other people, not just for yourself. On a stage, that saves lives.
lines.g_love_funny: You make me laugh, and I'm usually the one doing that. I'm almost jealous.
lines.g_love_brave: You climb first, every time, no fuss. Every good crew has one of you, and they're worth gold.
lines.g_love_steady: You don't panic when the load swings. That's the whole job, really, and you just have it.
lines.g_love_clever: You work out how things hold together, proper engineering. I'd trust you with the hard rigs.
lines.g_love_honest: You tell me straight when my knot's bad. I hate it every time, and I respect it.
lines.g_love_quiet: You don't talk during the work. That's rarer than a straight truss on tour, and I love you a little for it.
lines.g_love_fierce: You hold on when everyone else lets go. On a bad lift, that's who you want on the rope.
lines.g_love_warm: Hanging out with you is like the bar after the get-out, everyone tired and happy. I'd missed that.
g_loved: Careful, crew, I'll get a big head, and then I won't fit through the doors.
That's nice of you, really, and I'm going to pretend I'm not touched.
lines.g_hate_sharp: You always aim for the sore spot, on purpose. On my crew, people like that ended up on the night shift alone.
lines.g_hate_kind: Stop asking if my shoulder's okay, it's fine, it's been fine for twelve years. It just complains.
lines.g_hate_funny: Jokes are great, after the lift. During the lift, I need everybody's eyes on the load.
lines.g_hate_brave: You climb without looking, every single time. One day there won't be a tree to catch you, and I won't either.
lines.g_hate_steady: You check and check and check, and the show starts without you. At some point you have to commit the lift.
lines.g_hate_clever: You explain knots to me like I'm new. I've tied more knots than you've had breakfasts.
lines.g_hate_honest: Every thought comes straight out, no filter at all. Some things you say after the show, not during.
lines.g_hate_quiet: You never call out, and then you're upset nobody knew. On a crew, you call it, loud and clear.
lines.g_hate_fierce: Everything's a race with you, even unpacking. Rushing is how things fall.
lines.g_hate_warm: You talk through every single job, start to finish. I need to hear the creak before it snaps.
lines.g_respect: We don't get on, and that's fine, not every crew does. But your lift back there was clean, and I'll say so.
lines.g_call_out: That drop was yours, mate, sorry. I said hold, and you let go, and the whole rig came down.
lines.g_stung: Okay, fair, heard you. I'll go check some knots for a bit.
lines.g_concede: Your rig was right, and mine wasn't. I went over it twice, and it was my knot that slipped.
lines.g_nod: You too, nice work up there. No need to make a thing of it.
lines.g_callback_save: I haven't forgotten you catching me in that fight. Second time in my life something caught me, and the first was a tree.
lines.g_callback_clutch: You and me, last ones on our feet, swaying like bad scaffolding. Best get-out of my life, that.
lines.g_callback_callout: When you told me off that time, I sulked for a whole shift. You were right, of course, it was a bad knot.
lines.g_former_rivals: Early on, I'd have rigged you to the far end of the truss. Now I'd trust you on my rope.
lines.g_changed: I've been on this island three years, crew. Longest I've been anywhere since I was twenty, and I'm not even itching to leave.
g_unguarded: Since it's just the two of us, the truth about the fall. Forty feet into a tree, and the first thing I did was check my carabiner. Not my legs.
I hurt this shoulder on a truss in 2014 and worked the show anyway. It still tells me the weather. Best forecaster I know.
lines.g_clipped: Sure, whatever you reckon. I'll be checking knots.
lines.g_noticed_open: Whoa, listen to that, a whole speech, nobody had to pull it out. Keep going, crew, I'm enjoying this.
arg_ask: {player}, you call this one, please. I've done my explaining, and they're not listening.
Okay, {player}, you're the stage manager now. Make the call, and we both live with it.
lines.arg_backed_me: Cheers, {player}, I knew you'd see the load path.
lines.arg_backed_them: Fine, your call, I'll work it. I still think it doesn't hold.
lines.arg_stayed_out: Staying off it, eh? Smart, I would too.
lines.arg_always_their_side: It goes their way again, {player}, every single call. I'm not blind, just saying.
lines.arg_wallflower: Nobody's calling it, so I'll call it. My way, crew, and we go.
lines.arg_reject: No, {player}, sorry, I can't rig that one. I've seen how it comes down.
lines.arg_grumble: Still think my knot was the right knot. I'll shut up about it after this.
lines.arg_settled: Half right each, then, fine. Shake on it and back to work.
lines.seen_listens: You wait until people are done before you jump in, {player}. On tour, that was the rarest thing on any crew.
lines.seen_truth: You call it straight, {player}, no fudging. I can work with that, it's how a good stage manager talks.
lines.seen_jokes: When the lift goes wrong, you're ready with a joke, {player}. The old crews did that at four in the morning, and it got us through.
lines.seen_stays_out: You keep out of the arguments, {player}. Wise, honestly wiser than me.
lines.seen_biased: One of the crew always gets the good gear, {player}. Everybody on the deck can see it.
lines.seen_harsh: You can be rough on people, {player}. I've had worse stage managers, but some of this crew haven't.
lines.seed_right: Your notes after that mess of a fight, {player}, I didn't love them. I rigged it your way today, and it held.
lines.seed_remember: Still turning over what you told me when everything came down. Haven't decided yet.
lines.seed_wrong: I rigged it your way, {player}, and it held worse. Just letting you know, nothing more.
lines.talk_aftermath_near_death: Got a second, {player}? That one nearly dropped me, nearer than I'll let on to the crew.
lines.talk_aftermath_wipe: We all came down, the whole rig. Sit with me, and we go through it like an accident report, knot by knot.
lines.talk_aftermath_blame_self: {name} came down first, and I'm meant to see the weak point coming. That's my whole job, {player}.
lines.talk_aftermath_first_clear: Load-in to get-out, nobody hurt, everything stayed up. That's a perfect show, crew, and I'm buying.
lines.talk_development: Weird question, {player}, go easy. Have I changed? I keep catching myself making plans for next year, here.
lines.talk_relationship_hard_on: I've been riding {name} hard, I think. I'm fussy about safety, and it comes out wrong sometimes.
lines.talk_relationship_likes_me: Be honest with me, {player}. Does {name} rate me on the crew, or am I just the knot guy?
lines.talk_relationship_respect_hate: {name} drives me up the wall, {player}. But on a bad lift, they're the one I'd want on the rope beside me.
lines.talk_relationship_acting_off: {name}'s not right, {player}. They're carrying weight wrong, like a rig with a hidden crack.
lines.talk_confrontation_favour: Quick word, {player}, straight up. The good gear is always rigged onto {name}, and the whole crew's clocked it.
lines.talk_confrontation_dislike: I'll just say it, it's easier. Me and {name} can't share a rig, and I've stopped acting like we can.
lines.talk_confrontation_risks: We keep going up without a safety line, {player}. I'll climb anything you want, but I'd like to come back down.
lines.talk_confrontation_wrong: I got {name} wrong, {player}. Their rig was right and mine wasn't, and I want to say it before my ego gets involved.
lines.talk_confrontation_trust: Straight question, {player}. On the big lifts, I'm left on the ground. Is that the rig plan, or does the stage manager not rate me?
lines.talk_confrontation_decided: My kit got rerigged onto {name} behind my back. I'd have unclipped it myself, {player}, if you'd asked.
lines.talk_shrug_aftermath: I'll be fine, I always bounce. Usually off trees.
lines.talk_stings_aftermath: Not what I needed, that. I'll go check some knots.
lines.talk_lands_development: So you see it too, huh. Good, I'm not imagining it.
lines.talk_shrug_development: Maybe, maybe not, who knows. Ask me next season.
lines.talk_stings_development: Nah, that's not it, {player}. You've got the wrong end of the rope.
lines.talk_lands_relationship: Fair enough, yeah. I'll talk to {name}, properly.
lines.talk_shrug_relationship: Could be, could be not. A person's a harder rig to read than any truss.
lines.talk_stings_relationship: Scratch that, I never said it. And keep it off {name}'s radar, okay?
lines.talk_lands_confrontation: Fair, that's fair, I'll take it. Bit bruised, but I bounce.
lines.talk_shrug_confrontation: Copy that, {player}. I'll chew on it up a ladder.
lines.talk_stings_confrontation: Right, so that's how it is. Good, the load's clear now, {player}.
lines.talk_door_closed: Nah, I'm done with this one. I'll be up a ladder somewhere.
lines.arc_cracks: I caught myself building shelves in the lean-to yesterday, crew, actual shelves. I've never owned a shelf in my life.
lines.arc_turn: Eighteen years I wanted the next tour, the next city, the next big lift. Here I keep wanting to stay put, and it scares me a bit.
lines.arc_become: I'm staying, {player}, with this crew, on this island. Something I build is finally going to still be standing when I'm old.
lines.arc_failed: Ah, I've got itchy feet again, I can feel it. I'll stay for now, but my bag's packed by the door.
lines.alt_turn: I bragged about the fall again yesterday, and then a lift went wrong, and I froze. First time ever. Nobody laughed, {player}, and I'm glad.
lines.alt_become: I don't tell the falling story any more. I just check the knots twice, and I'm a better rigger for it.
g_roast_after: Still the messiest crew I ever worked, and I'd do every show of my life with you lot.
Bad knots, worse timing, and the only crew I'd ever settle down with.
lines.g_after_wipe_after: Up, everyone, together, check each other's gear. We came down, we get back up, and nobody's left on the deck.
lines.g_toast_after: To my crew, the first one I ever stayed for. I mean that, and I don't usually mean things.
lines.g_crew_after: This is my crew now, permanently. No next tour, no next city, just you lot and good knots.
g_quiet_line_after: I hung a door in the lean-to today, proper hinges. It's going to be there next year, and so am I.
Haven't thought about the next tour in weeks. Feels good, actually.
g_loved_after: Thanks, crew, really, no joke this time. I'll keep that one.
That's lovely, and I believe you. Feels like home, that.

history.open: I'll get this out of the way early, {player}, because it always comes out as a brag. I arrived forty feet in the air and landed in a tree. Walked away with a scratch.

options.reply: See, I tried to say it humbly, and it still came out like that. I've given up fixing the delivery.

options.text: What were you doing up there?
options.reply: Rigging a concert hall in Prague, four in the morning, up in the grid. Eighteen years of hanging heavy things over people who never looked up.
Afterwards, yeah, properly. During, I was just annoyed I'd dropped my good spanner.

history.open: People here build fast and tie off badly, {player}, and I physically can't walk past it. I fix scaffolding all over Fenris Isle, and they pay me in food and arguments.

options.reply: Because one day it falls on somebody, and I'd know I walked past. I've never been the reason something fell, and I'm keeping that record.

options.text: Sounds like you're the island's rigger now.
options.reply: Ha, nobody hired me, but yeah, I suppose I am. First steady gig I've ever had.

history.open: My parents are in Brno, {player}, or they were. Dad's a welder, Mum's a nurse. I moved to Prague at twenty and only went home at Christmas, which I regret now.

options.reply: Dad taught me knots before I could read, Mum taught me to look up before I walk under anything. Between them they made a rigger.
I hope so. I hope they're together, wherever Brno came down. That's the version I let myself think about.

friend.open: I've never settled with anyone, {player}. There was Dominik, a lighting tech, two years on the road, and he wanted a house and I wanted the next tour. Then Klara, a stage manager, and I never asked. The crew ran a book on it. I've started talking about both of them in the past tense.

options.reply: My friends here noticed first. I'm always the last to see the load shift, apparently. Even my own.

options.text: Maybe you're ready to settle now.
options.reply: Maybe I am, yeah. Here, with this lot. That's the first time I've said that out loud and not laughed.

sworn.open: On a crew, {player}, you clip in next to someone you trust with your life. I'd clip in next to you any day. That's the most I've got.

options.reply: Then we're tied off together, partner. Good knot, too, I checked.

options.text: Only if you check my knot.
options.reply: Always, every time, twice. That's what crew means.

reconciled.open: Me and {name} sorted it, properly, before the next lift like you're meant to. Wanted you to hear it from me.

options.reply: Cheers, it was overdue. Crew's tighter for it.
Me, obviously, I'm the one who fell out of the sky. It's the rule.
